mainTopic: Whether partial entry counts as entry, and the מצורע's סמיכה at שער ניקנור: which parts of סמיכה and תכף לסמיכה שחיטה are from the Torah
overview: This amud opens by closing an earlier discussion: both אביי and רבא hold that טומאה is only pushed aside (דחויה) for the ציבור, not fully permitted. The גמרא then returns to עולא's view that partial entry into the עזרה counts as entry. It offers a ברייתא as support: every סמיכה is followed right away by שחיטה, except a מצורע's, which happens at שער ניקנור because he may not enter yet. If reaching in with his hands were not 'entry', he could simply lean and have the animal slaughtered right there. רב יוסף rejects the proof: the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, for whom the northern slaughtering area is far from the gate, and the מקדש's design cannot be changed to add an opening. In another version, רב יוסף says proper סמיכה needs head and most of the body inside, so hands alone will not do. The גמרא then asks why the מצורע does not just go in, if the Torah requires both סמיכה and the immediate slaughter. רב אדא בר מתנה answers with a גזירה against extra steps. Another version says the immediate slaughter is not from the Torah. A ברייתא disproves that version, so the גמרא reverses it: the מצורע's סמיכה is rabbinic, while תכף לסמיכה שחיטה is from the Torah.

steps.title: Both אביי and רבא hold that impurity is only pushed aside for the public
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the previous discussion: both אביי and רבא hold טומאה דחויה בציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn from this that both of them hold that impurity is only pushed aside, not fully permitted, when the public is involved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the earlier argument between אביי and רבא. It points out a basic idea they both agree on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to understand why the ציבור may bring offerings while impure. One says טומאה is fully permitted (הותרה). The other says it is only pushed aside (דחויה), so some limits still apply. The גמרא notes that both אביי and רבא take the second view.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference; we can learn from this
both of them
impurity that is only pushed aside, not fully permitted
the public, the community as a whole

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא agree: for the ציבור, טומאה is דחויה (pushed aside), not הותרה (fully permitted).

phrases.english: By inference, both of them hold:
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means אביי and רבא from the discussion just before this.

phrases.english: impurity is overridden in the case of the public.
phrases.notes: 'Overridden' means pushed aside for now, not made fully permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier אביי/רבא discussion from before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי and רבא both hold טומאה דחויה בציבור.

steps.title: A ברייתא about סמיכה at שער ניקנור is offered as support for עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a ברייתא supports עולא. Every סמיכה is followed right away by שחיטה, except a מצורע's סמיכה, which takes place at שער ניקנור because he cannot enter yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say a source supports עולא: 'For every leaning of hands that took place there, I apply the rule that slaughter must come right after the leaning. The one exception is the leaning done at שער ניקנור, because a מצורע cannot enter there until the blood of his חטאת and אשם is sprinkled for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to עולא's rule that partial entry counts as entry. It quotes a ברייתא that might back him up. This step only sets up the source; the next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally סמיכה and שחיטה must happen one right after the other, in the same place. A מצורע is the exception: he leans on his אשם at the gate, outside the עזרה, and the animal is slaughtered later inside. The ברייתא explains why: he is not yet allowed to enter.

keyTerms.meaning: let us say this supports him
leaning one's hands on the head of an offering
slaughter must come immediately after leaning
the Nicanor Gate, the entrance to the Temple courtyard
a person with צרעת, a skin affliction that makes one impure

phrases.english: Let us say that a source supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is עולא, who said partial entry counts as entry.

phrases.english: All the placings of hands that were there
I apply to them
the rule that slaughter immediately follows the placing of hands;
except for this one, which was at the Nicanor Gate,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the מצורע leaning on his אשם.

phrases.english: since a leper cannot enter there
until they sprinkle on his behalf
from the blood of his sin offering and from the blood of his guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אביי/רבא topic and goes back to עולא's rule about partial entry.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's rule that ביאה במקצת שמה ביאה (partial entry counts as entry).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the מצורע's סמיכה at שער ניקנור being the one exception to תכף לסמיכה שחיטה.

steps.title: How the ברייתא proves that partial entry counts as entry
steps.stepSummary: If partial entry were not considered entry, the מצורע could reach his hands into the עזרה, lean, and have the animal slaughtered right there. Since the ברייתא does not allow this, reaching in must count as entering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say partial entry is not considered entry, then let him put his hands inside and lean!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why the ברייתא supports עולא. If putting in just his hands were not 'entering', the מצורע would have an easy way to keep the normal rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why must the מצורע be an exception? He could put only his hands into the עזרה and lean, and the animal could be slaughtered right there. The ברייתא still treats his case as an exception. That suggests putting in even part of the body counts as forbidden entry, which is exactly עולא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you say
partial entry, entering with only part of the body
let him put his hands in

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about where the מצורע stands. It is about whether simply reaching his hands inside would already count as forbidden 'entering'.

phrases.english: And if you say
partial entry is not considered entry —
let him insert his hands and place them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּיאָה בְּמִקְצָת לֹא שְׁמָהּ בִּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the proof from the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's exception only makes sense if putting in one's hands already counts as entering.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, so there is no proof
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He holds the northern slaughtering area is far from the gate, so the animal could not be slaughtered by the gate anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says the north is far away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on the proof. He shows there is a different reason the מצורע could not lean and have the animal slaughtered right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם must be slaughtered in the צפון, the northern area. According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, that area is only the space north of the מזבח, far from the gate. So even if the מצורע reached in and leaned at the gate, the animal could not be slaughtered there. The ברייתא's exception tells us nothing about whether partial entry counts as entry.

keyTerms.meaning: whose view is this?
the north is distant, far from the gate

steps.whatToRemember: The proof for עולא fails. The ברייתא's exception can be explained because, for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the slaughtering area is far from the gate, not because reaching in counts as entering.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a typical move in the גמרא. A proof is turned aside by showing the source can be explained by a different תנא's opinion on another issue, so עולא's rule stays without support from here.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: the north is distant.
phrases.notes: For him, the northern slaughtering area is only next to the מזבח, far from the gate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for עולא offered in steps 2 and 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not disprove עולא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's exception has another explanation: according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, slaughter could not happen at the gate anyway, since the northern area is far away.

steps.title: Why not make a small opening in the wall?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests making a small opening in the wall so the מצורע can reach through and lean near the slaughtering area.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them make a small opening in the wall!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's answer: even if the gate is far from the north side, why not cut a small opening in the wall near the slaughtering area so the מצורע can reach through there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the ברייתא can't let the animal be slaughtered right after סמיכה because the gate is far from the north. This challenge says a simple fix would let סמיכה and slaughtering happen right next to each other. If that works, the ברייתא's ruling still needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A small opening or wicket in a wall
But let them make

phrases.english: But let them make a small opening!
phrases.notes: He means an opening in the wall of the עזרה, near the slaughtering area, that the מצורע could put his hands through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer by offering a practical way around the distance problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's answer that the distance from the gate to the north is why the ברייתא doesn't allow slaughtering right after סמיכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If distance is the only problem, a wall opening near the north would solve it.

steps.title: The Temple's design cannot be changed
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא quote a פסוק showing the מקדש's layout was given by ה׳ in writing, so no opening may be added.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: "All this in writing, from the hand of ה׳ upon me; He made me understand all the work of the design."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא answer the challenge. The design of the מקדש came from ה׳, so we can't cut new openings in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that the plan of the מקדש was given exactly by ה׳. Adding an opening would change that plan, so this fix isn't allowed, and רב יוסף's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
Design, plan (of the מקדש)
In writing

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule: the structure of the מקדש is fixed by ה׳'s plan and can't be changed for convenience.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:
"All this in writing, from the hand of ה׳ upon me,
He made me understand all the work of the design."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about making a wall opening.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק rules out the suggested fix.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could just add an opening in the wall near the north side.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מקדש's design was fixed by ה׳, so no opening may be added.

steps.title: Leaning needs head and most of the body inside
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב יוסף explains that סמיכה must be done with full strength, so the person's head and most of his body must be inside. Just reaching in with the hands isn't enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב יוסף said: anyone who leans must bring in his head and most of his body. Why? Because we need all his strength. So it's not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of רב יוסף's answer to the proof for עולא. This time the reason is different: real סמיכה requires putting your head and most of your body in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof for עולא said: if reaching in didn't count as entering, the מצורע could just reach in and lean. This version answers that reaching in with only the hands isn't proper סמיכה at all, since סמיכה needs his full strength. So the ברייתא proves nothing about whether partial entry counts as entering.

keyTerms.meaning: His head and most of his body
All of his strength
Therefore

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion against רב יוסף; it is a second version of what רב יוסף said. It replaces the "north is far away" reason with a different reason.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rav Yosef said:
Anyone who leans must bring in his head and most of his body.
What is the reason? We need all his strength;
Therefore it is not possible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב יוסף's rejection of the proof for עולא, using a different reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what proper סמיכה requires, which removes the proof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that reaching in counts as entering; otherwise the מצורע would reach in and lean.
steps.terutzMaskana: Reaching in with the hands alone isn't valid סמיכה, so the ברייתא proves nothing about partial entry.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא for עולא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the hands alone could do סמיכה, but סמיכה needs head and most of the body with full strength.

steps.title: If it's all from the Torah, let him just go in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא holds. If both סמיכה on the מצורע's אשם and slaughtering right after סמיכה are from the Torah, the מצורע should simply go in and lean, since the Torah requires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he hold? If he holds that leaning on the מצורע's אשם is from the Torah, and that slaughtering right after leaning is from the Torah, then let him go in and lean openly, since the Torah said so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling that the מצורע leans outside at the gate. If the Torah itself requires both the leaning and the slaughtering right after it, why not just let him go in?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both rules come from the Torah, keeping them is a Torah command. So the מצורע should be allowed to go in and lean properly next to the slaughtering. The fact that the ברייתא keeps him at the gate needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he hold?
Leaning on the guilt offering (אשם) of a מצורע
From the Torah
Slaughtering must come right after leaning
Openly, outright

phrases.english: What does he hold?
phrases.notes: "He" is the תנא of the ברייתא who ruled that the מצורע leans at the gate.

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר סְמִיכַת אֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: If he holds that leaning on a leper's guilt offering is from the Torah,
and that slaughtering right after leaning is from the Torah,
let him go in and lean outright,
since the Merciful One said so!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר סְמִיכַת אֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 7: if reaching in with the hands alone is not valid סמיכה, why not let the מצורע enter fully, since the Torah requires it? It questions the ברייתא's ruling that he leans at the gate.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the מצורע leans outside at שער ניקנור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both סמיכה and slaughtering right after it are Torah rules, the Torah itself wants him to lean properly, so he should go in.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree against extra steps
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה answers that the חכמים made a גזירה keeping the מצורע out, out of concern that he will walk in more than needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said: it is a decree, in case he takes extra steps.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה answers: by Torah law he could go in, but the חכמים stopped him so he wouldn't go further inside than necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer accepts that both rules are from the Torah. The reason he stays outside is a rabbinic safeguard: if allowed in, he might take more steps than he needs.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Lest, in case
He will take extra steps

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said:
It is a decree, in case he takes extra steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַרְבֶּה בִּפְסִיעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of why the מצורע isn't allowed to go in.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If both rules are from the Torah, the מצורע should go in and lean.
steps.terutzMaskana: Torah law might allow it, but the חכמים kept him out so he won't take extra steps inside.

steps.title: Slaughtering right after leaning is not from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב אדא בר מתנה says that סמיכה on the מצורע's אשם is from the Torah, but slaughtering right after it is not. So he can lean outside at the gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב אדא בר מתנה said: leaning on the מצורע's אשם is from the Torah, but slaughtering right after leaning is not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב אדא בר מתנה's answer. Here he rejects one of the assumptions in the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed both rules were from the Torah. This version says the rule of slaughtering right after סמיכה is not from the Torah. So there is no Torah need to bring him inside: he leans at the gate, and the animal is slaughtered later in the north.

keyTerms.meaning: Not from the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Two versions of רב אדא בר מתנה explain why the מצורע leans at the gate: either a גזירה so he won't take extra steps, or because slaughtering right after סמיכה is not a Torah rule.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה:
phrases.english: There are those who say: Rav Adda bar Mattana said:
Leaning on a leper's guilt offering is from the Torah,
but slaughtering right after leaning is not from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב אדא בר מתנה's answer to the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects one of the question's assumptions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both סמיכה and slaughtering right after it are Torah rules, so the מצורע should go in.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the סמיכה is from the Torah; slaughtering right after it is not, so he may lean outside at the gate.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows slaughtering right after סמיכה must be from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version of רב אדא בר מתנה using a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns that שחיטה must be done by pure people, just like סמיכה. That only makes sense if סמיכה must be done right before the slaughter, inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'And he shall lean... and he shall slaughter.' Just as leaning is done by pure people, so too slaughtering is done by pure people. But if you say that slaughtering right after leaning is not from the Torah, you could also find leaning done by impure people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second version of רב אדא בר מתנה from step 10, using a ברייתא about סמיכה and שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes that סמיכה is only done by טהורים. That is true only because סמיכה must happen inside the עזרה, right before the slaughter, and a טמא cannot go in there. If תכף לסמיכה שחיטה were not from the Torah, a טמא could do סמיכה outside at the gate, and the ברייתא's comparison would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually pure people
Ritually impure people
Slaughtering the animal

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says outright that תכף לסמיכה שחיטה is from the Torah. The גמרא figures this out because the ברייתא takes for granted that only pure people can do סמיכה.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'And he shall lean... and he shall slaughter'
just as leaning is done by pure people,
so too slaughtering is done by pure people.
And if you say it is not from the Torah,
phrases.notes: 'It' means slaughtering right after leaning, the idea from step 10.

phrases.english: you also find it with impure people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version of רב אדא בר מתנה from step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תכף לסמיכה שחיטה is not from the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's comparison takes for granted that סמיכה is only done by טהורים. That is only true if סמיכה must be done inside right before the slaughter, which means תכף לסמיכה שחיטה is from the Torah.

steps.title: Reverse the version: the מצורע's סמיכה is rabbinic, and the immediate slaughter is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the second version. סמיכה on the מצורע's אשם is not from the Torah, while slaughtering right after סמיכה is from the Torah. This fits the ברייתא and still explains why the מצורע leans outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, reverse it: leaning on the guilt-offering of a מצורע is not from the Torah, and slaughtering right after leaning is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by switching which part is from the Torah and which part is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now תכף לסמיכה שחיטה is from the Torah, so the ברייתא works: סמיכה must be done inside, and only pure people can do it. The מצורע's סמיכה is only דרבנן, so the חכמים did not require him to enter the עזרה. He may lean outside at the gate.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it, switch the two parts around
The guilt-offering a מצורע brings when he becomes pure
Slaughtering must come right after leaning
From the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: In the final version, slaughtering right after סמיכה is from the Torah. סמיכה on the מצורע's אשם is only rabbinic, which is why he can do it outside at the gate.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the מצורע can lean outside the עזרה without breaking the Torah rule that the slaughter must come right after סמיכה.

phrases.english: Rather, reverse it:
leaning on the guilt-offering of a מצורע
is not from the Torah,
and slaughtering right after leaning
is from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by reversing the version given in step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סמיכה on the מצורע's אשם is from the Torah, and slaughtering right after it is not.
steps.terutzMaskana: סמיכה on the מצורע's אשם is rabbinic, and slaughtering right after סמיכה is from the Torah.
